name: dusty packed wasteland earth ground, a seamless 4x4-tile field with soft clumped earth with raised clods, gentle lighter dry and darker damp areas and small grit clusters running across tile borders
label: wasteland_ruins/dirt-a

answer.evidence: The image is a seamless full-bleed 96x80 field of earth texture. The silhouette is 96 wide on every row, with no outline, no edge line, no eave shadow and no front face. The column scans show only mottled light and dark clods, with no structural band. It is a flat ground texture that fills the tile area, which suits a terrain kind. By the rules it measures as a top-down surface with no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a brown earth field built from only 6 distinct colours, about 3 per tile. It reads as roughly 3 shade steps (light, mid, dark brown) plus a few sparse grit dots. The Beodeul grass reference also shows about 3 visible tones per tile, but it has 26 raw colours, with tufts, clumps and a lighter and darker patch. The paving reference reaches 7 tones with shaded stones. Near-flat coverage is 4% against 0% for both references, so there are few flat fills, and the blotchy clods break up the surface. There are no outlines, which is fine for ground. The shading is shallow, though. The clods are made of mid-to-dark blobs with minimal highlights, and the grit clusters are few and sparse. The result looks more like a noise-blotch pattern than the 5-6 step per-clump shading of the references. The candidate does not match the references' craft, and when in doubt the rule is fail.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a brown earth field with only about 3 visible tones per tile and just 6 distinct colours in the whole piece. The grass reference has 80 distinct colours and 26 per tile, though it also shows about 3 visible tones per tile. The candidate has soft clod blobs, lighter dry and darker damp patches, and sparse grit specks, with only 4% near-flat coverage, so it is not made of flat fills. Its shading is shallow compared with Beodeul's 5-6 steps per material: the clods are two or three brown shades with no highlight and no deep shadow ramp, and the grit dots are sparse. It has no outlines, and the dark edge pixels carry a brown tint (0% neutral). It reads as a blotchy two-tone camouflage pattern, not as shaded raised clods. Next to the references it looks thinner and flatter, since the paving reference reaches 7 visible tones and the grass has per-tuft highlight clusters. The measured facts match the grass reference only on visible tones, and the picture shows less structure than the grass. When in doubt, fail.

Visible tones per tile (3) equal the grass reference (3), but the grass reference has 26 raw colours of fine grain, while the candidate is made of broad blotches with only a few grit pixels. Overall it is flatter and less varied than the references. The clods lack highlight and deep-shadow steps, and the damp and dry areas are barely distinguishable. A careful artist would likely want more tonal steps and grain before accepting it next to the Beodeul grass and paving.
